newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria cautions against pinning hopes on talks.
newsitem.headline: Syria cautions against pinning hopes on talks.

text.p: Syria on Tuesday cautioned against pinning any hopes on a Middle East summit in Washington, saying it was impossible to advance peace if Israel did not change its policies towards Arabs.
"Without a dramatic change in the policy of the current Israeli government it is impossible to pin any hopes on any meeting," Damascus' state-run radio said in a commentary.

U.S. President Bill Clinton called the summit to discuss last week's clashes that erupted after Israel opened a tunnel near Jerusalem's al-Aqsa mosque, Islam's third-holiest site. Fifty-seven Palestinians and 15 Israelis died in the fighting.

The summit, opening later on Tuesday, will group Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat and King Hussein of Jordan. Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak turned down the invitation because he was displeased with Israel's attitude and actions towards the Palestinians.
The Damascus radio, which reflects government thinking, renewed its condemnation of Netanyahu's policies, saying the Israeli premier went to Washington with a tougher stand.
Netanyahu has rejected closing the tunnel.
The radio said Netanyahu's policies were endangering peace and stability in the Middle East and urged Clinton to pressure the Israeli leader to accept peace.
"Netanyahu headed to Washington carrying his rejection to withdrawal from the occupied Arab lands, refusal to stop settlement building and rejection to trade land for peace," the radio said.
"Without an effective pressure on Israel the region will move to a catastrophe," the radio said.
Syria has held sporadic peace talks with Israel since 1991 but no negotiations were held since Netanyahu won May elections, unseating the Labour-led centre-left government.

Syria wants Netanyahu, who opposes trading occupied Arab land for peace, to commit himself to pulling back fully from the Golan Heights, captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war, before talks are restarted.
